title: Mechanism Vocabulary And Discovery Library
description:
This is step M1 of the "mechanism wave" (W4, in the approved plan `/Users/ueli/.claude/plans/the-codebase-still-has-spicy-umbrella.md` — read it in full first, especially the "Mechanism changes" section and the M1 bullet under "Step 1"). This step is foundational: it must land and be verified green before anything else in the mechanism wave (M2-M9) or the framework wave (W8) proceeds, because everything downstream consumes what you build here.

CONTEXT — READ IN FULL, IN THIS ORDER:
1. `/Users/ueli/.claude/plans/the-codebase-still-has-spicy-umbrella.md` — the full plan for this and all following waves. Pay special attention to: the "Mechanism changes" section (decisions list + Step 1 through Step 12), the "Target architecture" section (final crate/package counts, area map, role markers), and the SHAPE V2 amendment at the top (the taxonomy shape rules you're encoding).
2. `.🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️08/☀️05/CRATE-CONSOLIDATION-AND-PLUGIN-TAXONOMY-RESTRUCTURE/📋️master.md` — the master tracking doc for the whole initiative (both this plan and its predecessor). Read it in FULL — it has ~15 hard-won lessons from ~35 prior plugin migrations you must not rediscover (systemic `Ok(`-corruption pattern, leftover-verification-overlay class of bugs, `#[path]` cumulative-resolution semantics, the DEVELOPER_DIR=/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools workaround, etc.) plus the current state of every completed plugin migration (all 32 + demonstrator are done as of this dispatch — only 🏗️fem is still in-flight under a different session, do not touch it).
3. `.🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️08/☀️05/CRATE-CONSOLIDATION-AND-PLUGIN-TAXONOMY-RESTRUCTURE/📋️TEMPLATE.md` — the per-plugin migration recipe (for context on the taxonomy shape you're formalizing into machine-readable form; you are not migrating a plugin, but you need to understand the shape deeply).
4. The existing registry script `🧰️framework/🛍️products/💻️os/🔨️modules/🔌️plugin/⚡️implementations/🟦️typescript/📇️registry/📜️script.ts` and root `📜️script.ts` (repo root) — read both in full to understand the CURRENT ad-hoc taxonomy logic (validateTaxonomyTree, validateConstitutionalCrates, LEGACY_LAYOUT_TOLERANT flag, the discovery regexes) that you are about to formalize and centralize. Do NOT refactor these scripts yet — that's M3/M4, separate future steps. Your job is ONLY to build the shared vocabulary + discovery library that M3/M4 (and later W8 framework-wave agents) will consume.

YOUR TASK: build ONE shared vocabulary JSON (`🔣️taxonomy.json`) and ONE discovery library (`🟦️discovery.ts`) in the repo's shared lib tree (`🧰️framework/🛍️products/🦑️repo/🔨️modules/📚️library/` — read its current structure first to place these correctly alongside existing shared lib code, matching its existing conventions). These become the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for:
- Taxonomy vocabulary: allowed role markers per ecosystem (`[package.metadata.semio]` for Rust, package.json `"semio"` key for TS, `[tool.semio]` for Python, project.json `metadata.semio` for Go), the roles enum (`plugin|framework|product|hub|s-module|extension|testkit|tool`), the SHAPE V2 tree-purity rules (per-language leaf file pattern e.g. `component.<ext>`, allowed `📦️packages/<lang>` structure — manifests only, entry file location, `#[path]` two-way base rules for Rust), allowed root-level data dir names (`📚️examples`, `🧫️fixtures`, `🤖️generated`) and root doc file names (`AGENTS.md`, `README.md`), forbidden path segments (both `⚡️implementations` and `⚡️implementation` spellings), and an area-maturity map replacing the current `LEGACY_LAYOUT_TOLERANT` boolean with an enum per area (`legacy|mixed|clean|exempt` — a package counts as migrated iff its `📦️packages/<lang>` dir exists, no hand-maintained lists).
- Discovery: one repo-wide `discoverPackages()` function that walks the repo and returns every package with its role, language(s), owner path, and maturity state — designed to be consumed identically by (a) the registry script, (b) root policy script, (c) a future Rust build.rs codegen step for the plugin SDK testkit (you do not need to write the Rust build.rs consumer yet — that's a later step — but design the JSON schema to be trivially consumable from Rust, e.g. plain JSON with no TS-specific types leaking in).

Resolve the "⚙️engine list disagreement" the plan mentions explicitly: the vocabulary needs to encode BOTH "artifact child dirs" (the taxonomy's structural children: 🔺️diff, 🗣️dsl, 🎒️pack, 🔧️op, 📡️spr, ⚙️engine) AND "completeness components" (which subset is REQUIRED vs optional for the taxonomy validator to consider an artifact complete) as two explicitly separate, named lists — don't conflate them.

Constraints from the shared rulebook (non-negotiable, read the master doc's "Registrar Protocol" section too):
- Do NOT refactor the registry script or root policy script yet (that's M3/M4, someone else's future ticket) — only build the new vocabulary+discovery files. It's fine (and expected) to leave the existing scripts as-is for now; they'll be migrated to consume your new files in a later step.
- Never touch root Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock, package.json workspaces, go.work, nx.json, .storybook configs, or any plugin directory.
- Never run git-modifying commands or use git worktrees.
- Do NOT use `run_in_background: true` for Bash commands you run yourself — run synchronously with generous timeouts (300-600s).
- Add tests for the discovery library against the CURRENT real repo state (it should correctly discover all 38 plugin crates + fem's in-flight state as "mixed", not error on it) — this is a strong go/no-go signal that your discovery logic actually works against real data, not just synthetic fixtures.
- Add any temporary files to your own ticket folder.
- When finished, call `mcp__repo__ticket_close` on your own ticket's exact path with a full summary (schema design, where discovery.ts landed, what you tested against) and the list of every file you touched/created. Do not touch any other ticket.

Report back a concise summary of the schema you designed and how you verified it against the real repo.
summary:
M1 (mechanism wave) — shared taxonomy vocabulary + repo-wide package discovery library.

SCHEMA (`🔣️taxonomy.json`, schemaVersion 2, plain JSON, serde-trivial: no heterogeneous arrays, nulls = Option). Extended the file that 26/08/05/TAXONOMY-VOCABULARY-AND-PACKAGE-DISCOVERY-CONTRACT + UI-ELEMENT-CO-LOCATION-RESTRUCTURE + SHAPE-V2-TREE-PURITY-BROADCAST had partially seeded, into the full M1 contract:
- ⚙️engine disagreement resolved as two explicitly separate, never-merged lists: `artifactComponentDirs` (COMPLETENESS set, 5 — what registry's validateTaxonomyTree requires) and `artifactChildDirs` (STRUCTURAL set, 6 incl. ⚙️engine — what root's POLICY_ARTIFACT_COMPONENT_DIRS allows). `artifactChildDirsExtra` removed (test-only consumer, updated). `validateTaxonomy()` enforces the superset invariant.
- NEW `ecosystems` map (per lang: manifestFilename, moduleRootFilename, marker {in/format/table/roleKey/idKey}, entryFilenames[], leafFilename, sourceExtension) — encodes all four role-marker locations: rust `[package.metadata.semio]`, TS package.json `"semio"`, Go `📋️project.json` `metadata.semio` (manifest is project.json, NOT go.mod — go.mod must stay at the owner root), python `pyproject.toml` `[tool.semio]`. dotnet declared but discovery-opaque (manifestFilename null).
- NEW `targets` map (⚛️react/🧊️wgpu/⌨️tui → lang + leaf/entry filenames) for the three-level `📦️packages/<lang>/🎯️targets/<target>/` shape.
- NEW `rustEntryPathRules`: cumulative `#[path]` resolution + BOTH valid conventions (`leaf-prefixed`: leaves get `../../`, `"."` resets untouched; `once-reset`: one outer `#[path = "../../."]`) — the bug only a real compile catches, now machine-readable.
- NEW packaging allowlist (`packagingFileNames` + `packagingFileSuffixes`) = "📦️packages holds packaging code only, never data"; NEW `artifactsDirName`/`appsDirName`/`modesDirName`/`windowsDirName` (single-sources registry's APPS_DIRNAME literal).
- NEW `areaStates` = legacy|mixed|clean|exempt + `packageMaturityStates` = clean|mixed + `migratedMarker` = "packages-dir-exists" (migration is derived from disk, never a hand list — replaces LEGACY_LAYOUT_TOLERANT).
- Kept every field the two un-refactored consumers read (artifactComponentDirs, windowChildDirs, taxonomyLeafFilenames, entryFilenames, libWiringLineBudget, packagesDirName, targetsDirName, elementsDirName, areas, forbiddenPathSegments both spellings, rootData*/rootDoc*) — M3/M4 switch them to `ecosystems`/`targets`; `validateTaxonomy()` makes the flat projections unable to drift from `ecosystems`.

LIBRARY (`🟦️discovery.ts`): one repo walk (`scanRepo`, memoized per repoRoot, `clearDiscoveryCache()` for tests) answering everything. `discoverPackages()` (role, lang, target, ownerRel, packageRel, manifestPath, id, area, derived maturity), NEW `discoverOwners()` (owner + langs/targets/roles + residualImplDirs + entryFilesAtOwnerRoot + maturity), `discoverPackageProblems()` (added `unknown-lang`/`unknown-role` kinds), NEW `discoverBurndown()` (impl-dir totals by area, mixed owners, markerless manifests, packaging violations), NEW `validateTaxonomy()`. `readSemioMarker()` is now ecosystem-driven (generic dotted TOML table + dotted JSON key path) so go/python work the moment a marker lands. Nested owners (draw's fsm, flow's bim extension, trinity's jack shell) are first-class owner rows.

VERIFIED AGAINST REAL REPO STATE (not fixtures): 43 packages / 41 owners / 34 clean / 7 mixed; zero discovery problems; plugin-role owners exactly equal the set of plugin dirs carrying `📦️packages/🦀️rust/Cargo.toml` (derived from disk in the test, no hand list). 🏗️fem's in-flight state is reported as maturity "mixed" (17 residual ⚡️implementations + Shape V1 owner-root 📦️lib.rs) and raises NO problem. Burn-down impl-dir count matches an independent `find`/independent test walker exactly (39 under ✏️s/🔌️plugins, 217-219 repo-wide; the one `find` extra is a generated `pkg/` dir, correctly skipped). Framework three-level targets resolve (ui → ⌨️tui/⚛️react/🧊️wgpu, renderer-engine → ⚛️react/🧊️wgpu). Tests: 21 new/updated in the existing 🧪️index.test.ts, suite 121 pass / 9 fail (baseline was 98/11 — both taxonomy failures fixed, the 9 remaining are pre-existing and unrelated). `tsc --noEmit` clean for 🟦️discovery.ts (the 3 errors reported are pre-existing in 📦️index.ts). Registry `check` re-run green through the change (38 plugin crates, 58 playgrounds, 7 framework packages); root `📜️script.ts policy` still runs its taxonomy rules through the lib (its exit 1 is 292 pre-existing high breaches from other migrations).

FINDINGS FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR (not fixed here — out of scope): (1) the W6 flow pilot deleted flow's legacy bim extension crate mid-run, so registry generated output is now stale (registrar duty, do not regen from a plugin/mechanism ticket); (2) flow's new `🧩️extensions/🏗️bim/📦️packages/🦀️rust/Cargo.toml` has a `[package.metadata.semio]` table with NO `role` key, and its nested path does not match registry's `findNewContractPluginManifestPath` regex either — so `flow-extension-bim` silently vanished from the plugin registry. This is exactly the plan's "Step 3 wrong discovery silently drops plugins" risk, live; M3 must switch registry discovery to `discoverPackages()` and the extension needs `role = "extension"`; (3) root `📜️script.ts`'s `policyDiscoverPluginCrateDirs` still requires an owner-root `📦️lib.rs` for `shape: "taxonomy"`, which is Shape V1 — under V2 it now matches only fem, so all four taxonomy policy rules are effectively dark (M4); (4) root `policyTaxonomyBarrelShapeBreaches` compares `pkg.area !== "taxonomy"`, a value outside `areaStates` — the equivalent state is "clean"; `validateTaxonomy()` will now reject it if anyone writes it into `areas` (flagged for the concurrent UI-ELEMENT-CO-LOCATION-RESTRUCTURE session); (5) burn-down currently lists 5 markerless package manifests (flow bim rust, trinity jack lsp, draw fsm + fsm macros, ui styling python) and 23 packaging violations (data/docs/Cargo.lock parked inside `📦️packages` dirs, incl. 3 leftover verification-overlay Cargo.locks in flow/reasoning/writer).
